subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures stay in the accepted-then-async lifecycle path with a typed terminal startup failure, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight Docker sandbox startup before returning accepted?
rationale: Both designs can address the reported silent hang, but the choice affects the public async spawn contract, registry state, gateway wait behavior, and the overlapping startup lifecycle issue.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal state that `sessions_history`, `subagents list`, and agent wait can show for Docker startup failures.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accept
options.body: Move enough Docker startup validation before the accepted response and reject immediately, accepting added latency and compatibility implications.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle tracker
options.body: Keep this issue as the sandbox-specific proof case while the broader lifecycle contract is settled in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal state that `sessions_history`, `subagents list`, and agent wait can show for Docker startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the sandboxed `sessions_spawn` contract points to this owner path.
